title: Sequence-tiered lazy-prefill and kernel-fit padding estimator
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduces sequence-tiered lazy-prefill and a kernel-fit padding estimator to reduce padding waste and KV prefill overhead; improves per-token cost and tail latency for mixed seqlen workloads.
commits: b2d8c9a: add kernel-fit padding estimator implementation
c3e7b11: integrate estimator into dynamic batch composer
d4f2aa4: add unit + perf tests, update docs
e5a9f88: tuning/benchmarks and CI flake fixes
description: Motivation: mixed sequence-length workloads still suffer from tail padding and unnecessary KV prefetch for short sequences that get assigned to large slots. This PR introduces two cooperating heuristics: 1) sequence-tiered lazy-prefill: instead of prefetching whole KV windows at enqueue time, requests are prefilled lazily based on an estimated chance they will be coalesced into a larger slot; tiers are computed by seqlen percentiles; 2) kernel-fit padding estimator: a lightweight estimator that predicts the actual kernel cost delta of padding a request from len L to L' (uses microbench-derived kernel cost curves per architecture) and exposes that score to the batch composer so padding tradeoffs are explicit. Changes include: new proto fields for tier thresholds, scheduler changes in runtime/scheduler/batcher.rs to add a tiered queue and lazy-prefill hooks, cache_manager updates to support on-demand KV prefill, a C++ pad_estimator module compiled for host and device builds, test harness updates and new perf benchmarks. Checklist: - [x] design doc (Linear ENG-4217) - [x] unit tests added - [x] perf benchmarks (bootstrap and multi-tenant) - [x] doc updates - [x] security review (KV prefill access controls) Commits: a1f3e7f: initial lazy-prefill scheduler scaffold; b2d8c9a: add kernel-fit padding estimator implementation; c3e7b11: integrate estimator into dynamic batch composer; d4f2aa4: add unit + perf tests, update docs; e5a9f88: tuning/benchmarks and CI flake fixes. Changed files (high level): runtime/scheduler/batcher.rs (tier queue, new enqueuing path), runtime/kv/cache_manager.rs (on-demand prefill API + metrics), runtime/kernels/pad_estimator.{cpp,h} (cost curve model + serialization), runtime/proto/batching_config.proto (tier config, estimator weights), tests/batching_perf.py (new scenarios and checker), docs/perf-tuning.md (how to interpret estimator scores). Review conversation highlights: Miguel: "Nice separation; can you ensure estimator weights are versioned with model releases so we don't mismatch kernels?" Author: "Added proto versioning and unit tests to validate weight compatibility at startup." Emily: "Benchmarks look promising, but one run showed tail p50 regression for 2048-length bursts" Author: "Tracked root cause to an aggressive tier boundary; added adaptive smoothing to avoid boundary oscillation." Liam: "Is there any KV leakage risk if prefill is delayed?" Author: "No; prefill uses current auth token and respects tenant isolation; added explicit audit log entries and tests." CI summary: linux-unit-tests (pass), windows-build (pass), perf-canary (pass after rerun), lint (pass), integration-sanity (pass). Performance notes: microbench curves collected on g5x and a100 show estimator-guided batching reduced average padding tokens by 11% and end-to-end per-token cost by ~8% on mixed 8k/512 seqlen workloads in our canary. Rollout plan: 1) behind feature flag for dedicated and hosted; 2) gradual ramp to 20% of traffic; 3) monitor pad_savings, kv_prefill_latency, tail_p99. Merge: squash merged into main 2026-03-04 by Miguel Torres. References: Linear ENG-4217, SUP-1084 (customer report), internal perf notebook [perf/redwood/seqlen-tiered].
notes: This PR focuses on runtime heuristics and includes minimal user-facing config surface; operators can opt-in via batching_config.tiers and estimator.enabled flag. Backwards compatibility: tier fields are optional and estimator defaults to safe fallbacks when no model curves present.
